utterances.text: Would you please use the pointer to indicate those positions.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Mr. President, perhaps the machine might zoom back to allow us a greater field of vision of the map. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D
utterances.text: [Indicates]

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Mr. President, I don't think -- yes, it is now picking it up.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I just didn't see that the sticker was on it, but I see it now.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sir, would you please indicate those positions on Ozrenska Street again.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D
utterances.text: [Indicates]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. How many times were you stationed in that area during the period that you were a member of the platoon?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D
utterances.text: Six or seven times.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When was the last time approximately that you were --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Ierace, in order to enable the Chamber to later on know where exactly the witness pointed at, could you please ask, since this is a copy to be marked by the witness, to mark especially Ozrenska Street.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Certainly, Mr. President. But before he does that, I have been advised by a member of my legal team that on an occasion I think Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. last week, you indicated that blue was the colour for the Prosecution, and black for the Defence, so I thought I --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I am mistaken. I have to look that up. But let me have -- perhaps Ms. Pilipovic, could you be of assistance? Blue was for the ... ?

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honour. Blue was for the Prosecution and black for the Defence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I'm very sorry to have created any confusion.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: I think there is a blue thick pen on the witness's table, Mr. President. So I'll invite him to use that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sir, could you please take the blue pen and mark the area of your positions on Ozrenska Street on the map in front of you -- to your right, I should say.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: And might the machine zoom back, Mr. President, if that could happen. No, the other way.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Zoom out, please. Yes.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Approximately when was the last occasion that you were stationed in that area?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D
utterances.text: In the winter of 1993. In February, I think. It was wintertime at any rate.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How many occasions all together approximately were you positioned there?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D
utterances.text: On six or seven occasions, each time we would stay for about five days but without interruption. And the last time we were there, we stayed only one night.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Mr. President, I ask that the witness be shown some photographs. It is P3251. Indeed, I think just that one photograph will suffice, since it has its own exhibit number, P3251. Before that, at one point, Mr. President, that will be placed on the machine. And for that reason, there's a signature that needs to be obscured. So perhaps the photograph could be shown initially to Ms. Harris. All right. Perhaps it could now be placed on the machine. Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sir, do you recognise the view which appears in the photograph before you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I think your signature appears on that page, together with a date placed by you. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were you present when the photograph was taken?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D
utterances.text: Yes, I was.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Where was the photograph taken from?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D
utterances.text: The photograph was taken from Ozrenska Street, or from a position which was perhaps just 2 metres away from that street.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was the photograph taken by an investigator of the Office of the Prosecution by the name of Johnathan Tait-Harris?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D
utterances.text: Yes, it was.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was the taking of the photograph following some directions given by you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Does the city of Sarajevo appear in the mid-ground of the photograph?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D
utterances.text: Yes, it does.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What is the --

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D
utterances.text: The urban area of the city, that is, with high-rise buildings.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What is the approximate direction that the camera was facing?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D
utterances.text: The camera was facing north.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In the foreground there appear to be some yellow- or orange-coloured piles of rubble; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Where were the positions on which you were located in relation to the foreground of the photograph?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D
utterances.text: Here, where this rubble is, was a house, a two-storey house, whereas our positions were some 15 metres below this house which was destroyed.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you refer to "our positions," do you mean the confrontation line or something else?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D
utterances.text: Yes. That's where the trenches were, the trenches where our positions were. That is where the trenches had been dug up, and we stayed in those trenches while we were there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: As of February 1993, how far were the confrontation lines from the trenches at this position?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D
utterances.text: Could you please repeat the question?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes. You've told us that there were trenches some 15 metres below the house which now appears as a pile of rubble. How far beyond those trenches were the confrontation lines, that is, the lines of confrontation with the other side, the forces of the other side?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D
utterances.text: The distance was not very great for sure; however, I couldn't be more precise. I don't know how far from us were the soldiers of the other side, because I never actually saw them. I cannot tell you specifically what the difference was between our trenches and their trenches, I suppose, because I couldn't see them. But because this is a slope, with a large number of private houses, I suppose, I assume, that they were very close.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You've told us that you placed a date on this copy of the photograph, that is, the 6th of July, 2001. How long before that date was it, approximately, that this photograph was taken in your presence?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D
utterances.text: Between seven and ten days before, thereabouts.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In the photograph, in the mid-ground, there appear some roofs of houses. In a general sense, were those roofs there in February of 1993?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D
utterances.text: I don't think that these roofs were there, because the whole area was riddled with bullets or burnt down in front of us. There were no roofs that were not damaged, like the ones that you can see on this photograph.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: On the occasions that you were positioned at Ozrenska Street, did you observe any members of the sniping unit operating from the same vicinity, that is, the sniping that you've told us about earlier?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D
utterances.text: Yes, I did. It was from this house whose rubble you can see on the picture that I was able to observe that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You said earlier the house was two storeys. Was there also a basement?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D
utterances.text: Yes. It had a basement and two additional storeys. It did not have a cellar.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: On the lower side of the house, given that it's apparent from the photograph it was built on a slope, was any of the basement exposed above ground level?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D
utterances.text: Yes. That is the ground floor that I spoke about, the ground floor plus two floors. So the house had the ground floor and two upper storeys.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I think you said earlier that you were positioned in a trench that was some 15 metres in front of the house. From your position, could you see any part of the snipers or any part of their weaponry protruding from the house behind you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D
utterances.text: Yes, I could clearly see that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: From time to time, did you hear the sound of firearms coming from the house?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D
utterances.text: Yes, I did, very often.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you ever see the equipment, if any, that the snipers had, that is, the snipers who were in that house?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What equipment was that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D
utterances.text: The equipment consisted of a very long-barrelled rifle. The barrel was much longer than the barrels that we had. This rifle also had telescopic sights, some kind of binoculars with a rubber eyepiece on it, which was at the end of the sights, plus they had binoculars and something like a telescope with which you had much greater visibility and you could see your target closer than normally. Apart from that, I also had an opportunity to see a special kind of machine-gun which had optic sights fitted on it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Had you seen that kind of machine-gun before?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D
utterances.text: What do you mean, "before"? You mean before the war or ...?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Before you saw it at the house at Ozrenska Street, had you seen that type of machine-gun?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D
utterances.text: Yes, I had, yes. I had seen this type of machine-gun before, and I had also seen sniper rifles at Grbavica before that, when snipers came to take up their positions.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You have told us that you heard the sound of firearms coming from the house. Was that single shots or automatic fire or both?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D
utterances.text: Single shots were fired from sniper rifles. As for this type of machine-gun that I told you about, mostly it was short, brief automatic fire. So yes, I heard both single shots and bursts of fire.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: During your periods in Ozrenska Street, did you ever speak to the snipers who were positioned there?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did they ever discuss the nature of their targets?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D
utterances.text: Yes, they did. They targeted civilians and soldiers alike.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: From where you were positioned, were you able to determine approximately the areas, that is, the physical areas, that they were targeting?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D
utterances.text: I was able to determine, that is, to assume where the physical areas are, by looking at the barrels. But I also had an opportunity to see the skyscraper which they targeted through binoculars which was right in front of us.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: From your observations, were you able to determine whether they targeted roads and intersections in particular?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D
utterances.text: The shooting was usually at the intersections and the transversals, as they were called, which were built horizontally around town and could be seen very well from those positions.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you please explain what you mean by a "transversal".

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D
utterances.text: They are broad roads down the width of the city, not longitudinally, and they form intersections with the vertical roads.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You've told us that you were there in February 1993. By that time, did you notice whether there were any barriers of any type that had been erected on intersections in the city?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D
utterances.text: Yes, I did. With binoculars, I could see some containers that had been set up to protect passersby who had to cross to the other side of the street. And they were sort of protection barrier from sniper fire or fire from this type of machine-gun or other weapons.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In spite of the existence of the barriers, did you make any observations as to whether those intersections still were targeted by the snipers in the house behind you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D
utterances.text: Yes, those places were targeted. And if you looked through a pair of binoculars, you could always see somebody going up to the container or passing by behind the container on his way to a building. You could see this with your binoculars. But sometimes people weren't as safety-conscious and would cross at points where there were no containers, and you could observe this clearly using your binoculars. You could see people passing by that way.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did the snipers ever discuss with you the targeting of persons at intersections where there were containers or other barriers?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D
utterances.text: Yes, they did. And they confirmed that they were targeting that kind of target.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I now refer you back to the photograph that you have in front of you, and I think on it you placed a red circle. Will you please wait while the photograph is placed back on to the machine so that we can all see the red circle. And can you indicate whether you placed that red circle on the photograph, that is, the original photograph?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What is the significance of the red circle?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D
utterances.text: The red circle signifies an intersection which was targeted from the positions I was deployed in.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You've told us that you were in Ozrenska Street as late as February 1993. Was that the case then? Was that the situation then?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D
utterances.text: Yes, it was.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Earlier you marked an area that is a length of Ozrenska Street as indicating the positions that you occupied. Were there other houses along the street, apart from the one the remains of which appear in the photograph, where you were also positioned?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D
utterances.text: Yes, there were.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I refer you again to February 1993, for instance. At that time, were there other houses to your left and right along Ozrenska Street which, to your knowledge, were occupied by members of sniping units?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D
utterances.text: You mean February 1993?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D
utterances.text: The last time I was there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D
utterances.text: No, they were only in that house.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What about on earlier times that you were positioned in Ozrenska Street? Were there other houses that also contained -- withdraw that. Was there more than one house? Were there more than one house that contained snipers?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D
utterances.text: Yes, there were, and they changed positions frequently. There would be several snipers, but they would also change their positions and move from one house to another and so on.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I suppose that made good sense as a defensive measure, according to your understanding. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You've told us that there were snipers - that is, members of the sniping unit - who occupied the skyscrapers down by the river. Did you ever see them with telescopes?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D
utterances.text: Yes, I did. They were there every day in those skyscrapers. They were always there, and they had the same equipment. But I never saw them Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. entering the skyscrapers with the machine-gun, just with the snipers.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Apart from the optical telescopes that you have told us about, did you ever see members of the sniping unit, either at Ozrenska Street or by the river, with different types of telescopic sights?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D
utterances.text: They had a separate telescope which was not mounted on the rifle. It was much broader, much wider, than the one on a rifle, and they were able to see the target better using this device.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you ever see sights that were apparently intended to operate in poor light conditions, that is, in the possession of members of the sniping unit?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D
utterances.text: Yes. They had the so-called infrared ones.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Mr. President, I don't intend to ask any more questions about the photograph which is presently before the witness, so that particular photograph might be removed from the machine. I will, in a few moments, be asking questions about the other photographs. I ask now that the witness be shown another exhibit, namely, Exhibit P3638. By way of description, it is a photocopy of pages from a manual of various firearms. We're in the process of covering up the witness's name which appears from time to time on the pages in the form of a signature, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: To save time whilst that's being done: Sir, in June 2001, were you shown a booklet depicting various small arms and other military equipment by investigator Jonathan Tait-Harris?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D
utterances.text: Yes, I was.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were you invited to go through the manual and indicate, by a tick, any weaponry that you had observed to be in the possession of your fellow soldiers whilst you were a platoon member?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you do that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you date and sign each of those pages?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: That is the pages upon which you recognised such equipment?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D
utterances.text: Yes. Yes. That's what I meant.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were you also shown, apart from small arms, a number of photographs of much larger equipment, such as troop carriers, tanks, APCs, and the like?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D
utterances.text: Yes. I was shown photographs of that nature too.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In a similar way, did you indicate one of those items as being one that you had observed to have been in the possession of the military with which you served in 1992 and 1993?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Mr. President, I ask that the witness be shown a copy of that exhibit, that is, Exhibit P3638, which has the names covered, and I ask that the witness place the last page on the viewing machine, to enable the Chamber to view the top half of that page. It might be drawn further down.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, please, Counsel.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Yes. Thank you. If you could stop there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Having regard to my earlier questions and your answers, sir, I take it that the machine which appears at the top of the page in three separate photographs was one that you recognised?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What did you call that type of machine?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D
utterances.text: An armoured APC, armoured personal carrier.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Now, in relation to the small arms, do you recognise any that you saw in the possession of members of the sniping unit?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In order to help you with that, would you -- to assist you in that activity, would you indicate to the usher the page on which those items or item appears, and then we can see them one by one; or if there's only one, just the one. I think on the machine we now have page 1344. I'll refer to the last four digits of the number at the top right-hand corner. I take it from your answer that you saw that -- one of those two small arms in the possession of the members of the sniping unit. Is that correct? If you could answer that question. Yes? And which of the two was it? The M-70B1 or the M-70B2, or both? I withdraw that. I just realised I'm on a different page. I think you placed a tick alongside each of the two weapons; is that correct? Have you placed a tick alongside each of the two weapons which appears on that page?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D
utterances.text: Yes. Both are ticked. But the snipers used weapons shown on the upper half of the picture.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I think that weapon is indicated as being an M-76. Is that so?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Mr. President, I do intend to tender this document. I apologise for not having indicated that earlier. I now move on to another one of the maps, and might the witness be shown Map 5. I think the usher has a copy which has the signature covered. Could that please be placed on the overview machine.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sir, was this also a map on which you placed markings in February of 1997?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And was that in response to being requested to indicate where you had seen various mortars, tanks, Howitzers, and APCs?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you do that by placing an "A" where you had observed an APC?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did these markings indicate positions where you had observed an APC at some stage between the commencement of a war in April 1992 and when you left Sarajevo in May of 1993?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: For the benefit of the Chamber, with the pointer, would you please indicate those positions, that is, where the letter "A" appears.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D
utterances.text: [Indicates]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes. All right. Now, did you use the letter "T" to indicate either a tank or groups of tanks that you had observed in the same period?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Would you please with the pointer indicate where you placed the "T."

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D
utterances.text: [Indicates]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I think you've just indicated five positions. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D
utterances.text: I apologise, but I didn't count.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. In any event, I'll take you back to the last position you indicated. Could you please point to it again.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D
utterances.text: [Indicates]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Did you use the letter "M" to indicate where you had observed in the same period either a mortar or a group of mortars?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Please indicate where you placed the letter "M" with the pointer.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D
utterances.text: [Indicates]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you use the letter "C" to indicate where you had observed a cannon?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Please point to where you have placed the letter "C." And in fact, this is in relation to the same period, I take it, the same period of time?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D
utterances.text: Yes. [Indicates]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you use the letter "H" to refer to Howitzer?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Would you please indicate where you placed the letter "H" to refer to Howitzers, I take it, in the same period of time.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D
utterances.text: [Indicates]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And were those observations made by you in the same period of time, between April 1992 and May 1993?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, is this the position that having regard to the topography, there was no line of sight from the -- I'll withdraw that. Having regard to the topography, was there a line of sight from the position where you marked the Howitzers to the city?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D
utterances.text: Yes, there was, in the distance far away.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you refer to cannon, could you explain what type of equipment you meant by that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D
utterances.text: The "H" denotes the guns that I thought were Howitzer-type guns.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: One of the positions in which you have marked a tank appears in the vicinity of the Transit Road. Could you please point to that T so that the Trial Chamber can see it.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D
utterances.text: [Indicates]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And could you tell the Trial Chamber the circumstances in which you made observations of a tank or tanks at that position.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D
utterances.text: This position from which the tank fired can be seen from my parents' apartment where I was living. And the tanks, when they were not active, were parked in -- close by to my parents' apartment. So I could always see them leaving and coming out on this Transit section, when they were going out to begin operation. And I could see with my bare eye when the actual shooting was taking place. And the same applies to the APC, which was parked in front of my parents' apartment block throughout the time that I was there, which means from April 1992 to May 1993.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How often throughout that period would you make those observations of the APC and the tank or tanks moving from the parking position to the Transit Road and then firing?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D
utterances.text: Fairly often. Two or three times a week perhaps.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You've told us earlier that that part of Grbavica was on a slope transgressed by the Transit Road. Was the parking place lower or on the same level or higher than the Transit Road from which it fired?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D
utterances.text: The place they were parked was lower with respect to the positions they opened fire from, being tanks or APCs.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sorry. If you could imagine being in that apartment and looking towards the?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D
utterances.text: Looking from the apartment window, the tanks were parked to my left, and the place the APC was parked was directly underneath the window of the apartment I was living in.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were you able to hear the tank or tanks or the APC when they started their engines from within the apartment?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D
utterances.text: Yes. You could hear it very well, and we always had to open the windows because of that, because unless they were, the glass would be shattered by the explosion.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Again, imagining that you were in the apartment, looking towards the city, was the position from which they fired in front of you or behind you or to the left or to the right, approximately?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D
utterances.text: It was in front and slightly to the left. In front and slightly towards the left. But I should like to stress that the tank moved about. It moves when it fires, which means that sometimes it was in front, sometimes it was behind, sometimes it was right up front, and sometimes it was more towards the left.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was that as you faced towards the city from within the apartment or in a different direction that was in front sometimes? Perhaps I'll rephrase the question. If you look at the map and imagine that you are facing north and that the top of the map is north, then if you imagine being in the apartment, did the tank and APC fire from a position south of you or east or west or north, that is, north of the apartment?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Piletta-Zanin.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, I have an objection to make. We don't know if the map, which is only a partial section, has a north somewhere. Where exactly is north? And this would be leading the witness with respect to this question. I see no trace of north anywhere on the map. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. The objection is sustained, although there might not be much confusion, having looked at other maps already used which are covering similar areas. Mr. Ierace, would you please rephrase your question.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: If you imagine being in your parents' apartment and looking towards the city, what direction were you looking, having regard to the points of the compass?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D
utterances.text: When I was at the window, I would be looking southwards. When I looked straight ahead of me, that would be south. West was to the right of me, and so on.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. And when you looked south from the apartment, what could you see?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D
utterances.text: I could see, as I said a moment ago, a tank or an APC at the Transit, firing from that point.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And if you turned around and looked north out of the apartment, assuming there was a window there, what would you see, generally, in a northwards direction from the apartment?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D
utterances.text: Northwards I would see the city, part of the city, which was being fired at.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Ierace, we are already one or two minutes over 1.00. If there's a suitable moment to stop your examination.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Mr. President, this would probably be as suitable as any other. I have a number of questions still to go on this area.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you very much. May I then bring a few issues to the attention of the parties. First, the Chamber would like to be informed about the problems about the witness pseudonym list. The second issue is that this Chamber has a bit more flexibility on the scheduling as we could -- as we would know before, and we would like to know whether the parties have any objections against -- Madam Registrar asks my attention. One moment, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Whether there are any serious objections against starting again at 9.00 in the morning and have the long morning sessions. It has been stressed by many people working in this courtroom that if we continue during the morning, that we have not a day split up in various Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. portions, but we'll sit in the morning and we'll have time available to prepare for the next day. So what we'll do is we'll start at 9.00 in the morning. But, of course, since it has been otherwise scheduled, if there are any serious objections, I'd like to hear them now, although my flexibility is limited. I have one specific question to Mr. Piletta-Zanin. I noticed that he arrives Monday in the morning, so if he would oppose against having the same schedule on Monday, we could perhaps use Monday for different portions, starting at 9.30 and then go on until 1.00, and then start again at 2.30 up until 4.00. I had this in mind because I imagined that you might have some difficulties in being here on time if we started at 9.00 in the morning, but please inform us if it's otherwise.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, thank you for asking. On Monday is my travelling day, so I would be very appreciative if we could begin on Mondays at 9.30. But I leave it up to you. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We see that there might be considerable problems for you, and so therefore you have a new Scheduling Order, but at least this week we'll start, then, the coming days, the coming four days, at 9.00 in the morning and continue until a quarter to 2.00, even perhaps to 2.00. So then we can adjourn now until 2.30. --- Luncheon recess taken at 1.05 p.m. 23 24 25

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Ierace.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Mr. President, I'm happy to report that I met with Mr. Piletta-Zanin and Ms. Pilipovic during the break, and I have provided them with copies of the motion by the Prosecution dated the 30th of October, 2001 seeking protective measures together with the annexure which sets out the details. It seems that the copy which they had was provided by a different part of the Tribunal to the OTP. It appears to be a translation into French of an annexure, and that appears to be the source of the confusion. So that seems to be -- we're now working off the same sheet of paper.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, that's marvellous, Mr. Ierace. So we're informed, still the schedule attached to the motion is guiding us for the future?

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: That is guiding us, Mr. President. If there are any additions to that, I will inform my friends this afternoon. We have spoken as to a meeting this afternoon after court where we will discuss also exhibits for the remainder of the week.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, okay. Thank you. Mr. Piletta-Zanin.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, we did, indeed, have some problems, but we had a meeting with the Prosecution and discussed them. The documents that we have now and that we base ourselves, being one of the languages of the Tribunal, is what we base ourselves on. So we thought that we were revisiting, if I could put it that way, the list of the Prosecutor. Now, I would like to be sure, and could Mr. Ierace confirm that for us, that there have not been any further changes because we see that certain names were deleted in the most recent list that we have received which are not to be found in the old list. So the people mentioned in this latest list might reappear. Anyway, perhaps Mr. Ierace could clarify the situation. I'm referring to Witness K, in particular, who is on the list of the 13th of December, 2001, and that is not the same Witness K who was on the list that we're going to work -- that was the old list dated the 30th of October, 2001.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could you please sort this out during one of your meetings and inform the Court about your findings. I think that's -- so let's not spend any time on it now, but it's good to know that still some work has to be done. Apart from that, I inform the parties that tomorrow for reasons -- for personal reasons, Mr. Galic, we'll finish tomorrow at 1.00 and not a quarter to 2.00, and we start at 9.00. Then I think we dealt with all the practical issues. Yes, Mr. Ierace, you've got another one?

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Yes, just one further one, Mr. President. The Defence has now filed a response to the motion by the Prosecution seeking leave to call witnesses via videolink.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, I've seen that.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: I would be grateful if at some stage this week, if it please the Trial Chamber, that issue could be dealt with.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I received it this morning. Of course, we will have to confer among the colleagues on how to proceed, whether there will be oral hearing or not. But at least we received the response of the Defence, and you'll hear from us this week. Those were all the practical matters. Then please, Mr. Ierace, proceed in the examination-in-chief of Witness D.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President. Might the witness again be shown the photographs, which are Exhibit P3251 through to P3255. I would ask that Ms. Harris be permitted to approach the usher and place some yellow stickers over the witness's name wherever it appears in the photographs.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sir, before the lunch break, you told us in summary that when you were in your parents' apartment and looked south, it was possible for you on occasions to see the tank or APC in position, that is, ready for firing. From the same apartment, if you were able to look north, you would see the city of Sarajevo, and facing in that direction it was to your left and straight ahead, that is, north of the apartment, where the vehicles were parked. Would you please now look at Annexure C. That is a photograph which appears to show some apartment buildings. Do you have that in front of you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is this also a photograph that was taken in your presence in about June of the year 2001?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was the photograph taken by investigator Jonathan Tait-Harris?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D
utterances.text: Yes, it was.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did that follow upon some directions from you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D
utterances.text: Yes, it did.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Have you placed a blue oval-shaped circle on the photograph?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D
utterances.text: Yes, I have.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: At the time that the photograph was taken, was the photographer standing on a road or off a road or near anything else?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D
utterances.text: By the road, on the raised area.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What was the name of the road?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D
utterances.text: The Transit, or bypass.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Approximately in what direction was the camera facing at the time the photograph was taken?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D
utterances.text: North.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What does the blue circle indicate?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D
utterances.text: The circle indicates the windows of the building I lived in.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Given that the photograph was taken in June, it follows that it was taken at the height of summer; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D
utterances.text: That's correct, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were the trees -- I withdraw that. Were the trees that produced the foliage in the photograph deciduous? In other words, were they trees that lost their leaves in winter?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D
utterances.text: Yes, they were.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In 1992 and 1993, were there trees in the same position as those which appear in the photograph in the area of the blue circle?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D
utterances.text: No, there weren't.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: From the apartment, what was the degree of view, if any, that you had of the road in the area where the photographer was standing when this photograph was taken? I should add, in 1992 and 1993.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D
utterances.text: The view was much better, because the trees that we can see in the photograph now were not as tall, and the house on the left and right were built on subsequently; they were added. That is to say, another floor or two were raised. They weren't as high, so the view was much broader and better than it was when this particular photograph was taken.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You've told us that -- I notice that Mr. Piletta-Zanin is on his feet.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Piletta-Zanin.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I don't think I heard the witness indicate a moment ago, before the question was asked of him, that he had already been in that house, or rather, that apartment. So the question which began, "From the apartment," the words "from the apartment," seems to be to be premature, if I can put it that way, the cart before the horse, so to speak.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Ierace.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: I'll clarify that, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You have identified an apartment as the significance of the blue circle. Whose apartment was that in 1992 and 1993?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D
utterances.text: (redacted)

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: This morning you said that at one stage [redacted]

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Ierace, before we continue, the question just put to the witness upon the objection of Mr. Piletta-Zanin, don't you think it should be redacted, in view of the protective measures?

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Yes. Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, this part will be redacted because it's -- it might not make the protective measures as effective as they should be. Please proceed -- Mr. Piletta-Zanin?

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Precisely so, Your Honour. The Defence agrees entirely.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: So you may proceed, Mr. Ierace, and we'll prepare the redaction.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So you've told us that when you looked south from the apartment, you could see on occasion a tank or an APC. Where did you make such a sighting in relation to where the photographer was standing at the time this photograph was taken?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D
utterances.text: I saw that from the window of the apartment, which is in the oval circle.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: On those occasions, on any of those occasions, was there a tank or APC in the position of the photographer at the time this photograph was taken?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Mr. President, at this stage, I would like the witness to view a portion of videotape which is presently marked as MFI-8. The audio-visual unit has it. I understand it has been keyed to the relevant position. I can indicate that that position -- I can indicate firstly that it is a portion of the videotape that was shown during the opening, which is titled "SRK Tank Fire." I ask that that video be shown. It takes approximately 15 seconds, I think, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. The video may be played.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sir, please watch the video which appears on the screen in front of you. It may be that the machine has to be adjusted.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Might the playing stop there. I would ask it be rewound and played again. And at an appropriate point, I will ask that the image be frozen; in other words, that the pause button be pushed.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Pause there, please.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sir, do you recognise the area which appears in the image on your screen at the moment?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Mr. President, for the purposes of the transcript, I'll describe the image as comprising various buildings including a block of apartments of at least five storeys. In the centre of the image is what appears to be an overpass or a bridge on top of which is a tank which has apparently made a discharge. There appears to be a large ball of flame protruding from the end of the barrel. The tank faces to the left of the screen.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sir, where is that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D
utterances.text: That is on the bypass, the Transit. It's the same street, the one we mentioned a moment ago, the one that you could see from the window of the apartment.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you mean by that the street upon which the tank is positioned on the image?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D
utterances.text: Yes, that's the street I mean. It's the same one.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Having regard to your earlier evidence about the slope, it would follow that the camera appears to be north of the position facing approximately south. Would that appear to be the case to you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D
utterances.text: Yes, it was taken. That is to say, the position from which this was taken, the tank would be on the south side. If you looked at it from the angle of photography, the person taking the photograph would be northwards, and the tank would be southwards facing.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Having regard to the colour of the foliage, in particular the tree foliage, are you able to estimate the season this was taken?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D
utterances.text: I think it was autumn, early autumn.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: As one looks at the image, where was the apartment we referred to earlier? In other words, does it appear in the image firstly?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D
utterances.text: No, you can't see the apartment on this photograph.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: As one looks at the image, was the apartment to the left or the right or above or below?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D
utterances.text: To the right.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is there anything about the image of the tank firing on the Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. Transit Road which appears in front of you which is inconsistent with what you observed from time to time in the same area?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D
utterances.text: No major difference. But from the window of [redacted], you can't see this particular position.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: I ask that the showing of the video continue for another few seconds. I will again indicate when to pause the machine.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Pause, please.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sir, did you notice just before the pause, there was what appeared to be some smoke issuing from the top of the tank, perhaps consistent with the firing of a smaller weapon?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D
utterances.text: Could you repeat that question, please. I apologise, but I didn't quite follow.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes. Perhaps whilst I repeat the question, the tape could be rewound slightly to approximately the point of the last pause and prepared for reshowing. Would you please watch the video, and in particular take note of the part of the tank which houses the barrel and look for any signs of what appears to be smoke. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Video could be played again.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: And pause again, please.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you make that observation?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D
utterances.text: Yes. You can see the smoke and the fire coming out of the barrel.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you notice some other smoke coming from the same part of the tank, perhaps consistent with fire of a smaller-calibre weapon?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D
utterances.text: I assume that that was the smoke issuing from the explosion.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Piletta-Zanin.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, objection. On the one hand, we keep repeating the video footage to facilitate the position of the witness, but I don't see how we can ask a question as to the calibre of a weapon that we see on a video clip.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I think that the question is leading to the extent that apart from firing of the tank, that also the attention is drawn to another weapon, and to that extent leads the witness into some kind of an answer. So the objection is sustained.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President. Having regard to the last answer, I won't pursue it. Returning to the video, if we could, would you please continue to play the video - this is directed to the audio-visual unit - until I again say "Pause."

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Pause.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you recognise that part which now appears in the image in front of you, that is, the buildings and so on, as to the area?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D
utterances.text: Yes, I do recognise it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Where is that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D
utterances.text: That's that part, the bypass, the Transit road, and the part the tank is on now, you can see that from the window that I mentioned a moment ago, the window of the flat.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: On the video, the vehicle appears to be travelling from the left to the right. In relation to the observations you made, having discharged its weapons, what did the tank or tanks or APC then do?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D
utterances.text: After opening fire, it would always move either forward or back, to the next firing, and then the whole process would be repeated again.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Having completed firing, what then would the vehicles do?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D
utterances.text: As I've just said, they would either continue to fire or the tank would go back down the Transit and down Vrace to the place the tanks were parked.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Having regard to the image in front of you, in which direction would they proceed when they returned down to the parking area?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D
utterances.text: They would move right. Looking at the image from this aspect, they would move right and then downhill, and go as far as Radnicka Street.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is there anything inconsistent with the video before you and your recollection of how the tank or APC would retreat to the parking area?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Piletta-Zanin.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, with all due respect to the Chamber, I think we ought to specify what period we're talking about, because I don't remember having seen a date at all in the transcript. I'm referring to this tank movement.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could you be more precise perhaps, Mr. Ierace, although when I still think of the question, inconsistency of what the witness saw might be at a different moment, but please see whether you can meet the objection or not.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Certainly, Mr. President. I did mention the period of time at the beginning of this line of questioning, but I'll certainly repeat it. Indeed, I'll do it in a non-leading fashion.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What is the period of time - that is, between what dates approximately - did you observe a tank or an APC fire from the vicinity of the Transit road?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D
utterances.text: From the period when I entered the army until the time at which I departed, I often saw either a tank or an APC at that position.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I think you said earlier that you entered the army on the 22nd of June, 1992 and you departed around, I think it was, the 10th or at least mid-May of 1993. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Now, you've told us that you also saw APCs fire from the same vicinity. What type of weaponry did you observe an APC to fire from that area?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D
utterances.text: Are you referring to APCs alone or to tanks as well?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: APCs alone.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D
utterances.text: They had long barrels at the front. I don't know exactly what the calibre was. And on the dome, on the turret which is on the APC, they had another machine-gun of a slightly smaller calibre.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In what circumstances have you seen an APC in the vicinity of the Transit road fire its weaponry in relation to the hatch? In other words, have you seen the weaponry fired with the hatch opened or closed or sometimes either?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D
utterances.text: The hatch was closed.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you have any knowledge as to the accuracy of which firing -- I withdraw that. Do you have any knowledge as to whether, with the hatch closed, the operators of the weaponry of an APC are able to hit their target with any accuracy? In other words, is there any impediment to their vision of the target area?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D
utterances.text: I don't think so.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you have any knowledge as to the accuracy of the guns which are placed on an APC, that is, which are part of their armoury?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D
utterances.text: I think they are very precise guns.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Mr. President, I ask the witness again be shown Exhibit P3638, that is the excerpts from the small arms manual. In fact, it's probably preferable that the witness is shown the copy I have because it's the one with the coverings.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sir, would you please turn to the page which has the numbers in the top right-hand corner 02081348.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Could that be placed on the overhead viewer.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I notice that the image has a tick alongside it. Did you place that tick there?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Beneath it there appear to be some words written in B/C/S. Do you know who wrote those words?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D
utterances.text: [No interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sorry. Could you repeat your answer, please.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D
utterances.text: Yes, I wrote that.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Mr. President, perhaps the overhead viewer could pan back so we could see all those handwritten words. All right.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: I thank the usher.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you read out those words that you wrote, please.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D
utterances.text: Says -- it mentions the calibre of this machine-gun. It's 7.92. And then it says it was also available, so that means that this weapon was also available. And we popularly called it the "seller of death."

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you ever see that weapon fitted with a telescopic sight, that is, when in the position of fellow members of your platoon or the sniping unit, members of the sniping unit?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D
utterances.text: Yes, I saw it with a sight.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In whose possession was it when you saw it with a sight?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D
utterances.text: I didn't see it in the possession of soldiers who were from my platoon. I saw other soldiers who didn't belong to my platoon with this sight.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Where were they when you saw it?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D
utterances.text: I had the opportunity of seeing them at positions in Ozrenska Street. I also saw them on several occasions in Grbavica. I saw several soldiers who had this.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You gave evidence this morning that while stationed at Ozrenska Street, you observed sniper-unit members with a rifle that you described as having a long barrel. Do you see that rifle anywhere in the pages of the manual before you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Would you please indicate what page it appears on, referring to the numbers in the top right-hand corner of the relevant page?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D
utterances.text: It's page 1344, page 1348.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: I would ask that the relevant page be placed on the overhead viewer.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I think you said there were two pages, 1344 and 1348. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: First we could place page 1344. I think the full name is 02081344. Place that page on the overhead viewer. All right.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And which of the two weapons is it, that is, the two weapons which appear on that page?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D
utterances.text: You can see a sniper weapon on this page.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I think there is one weapon -- the two weapons are placed on top of each other, one on top of the other. Is it the one towards the top or the one towards the bottom?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D
utterances.text: It is the one on top.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. And I think that that is described in the text as being an M-76. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: I would ask that the usher now place page 02081348 on the overhead viewer. And perhaps it could be moved down the page. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And that weapon, according to the text on the manual, is described as M-84. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D
utterances.text: Yes, this weapon is called an M-84 machine-gun.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Ms. Pilipovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, the counsel has an objection to the examination of this witness with regard to weapons. The objection relates -- is because my honoured colleague should ask the witness to first provide a description of the weapon and ask him whether he knows what it looks like, in any case, and then specify that this weapon is in question, and not to first show him a picture of this weapon. We don't know whether the witness knows what an M-84 is and what it looks like. He should first tell us what an M-84 is; he should describe it; and then indicate it on the picture.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Ierace.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Mr. President, the issue is not whether it's known as an M-76 or an M-84, but rather whether the witness in around June 2001 made an identification of particular pieces of weaponry from a manual that he was shown. Nothing hangs on the name or the numbers or the letters by which in some circles the weapon was identified.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The objection is denied.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sir, you have now indicated two rifles. And earlier you described seeing one particular rifle with a long barrel. In indicating the two rifles, what is it that you mean to suggest? In other words, you saw both or you saw one, or it was something like that, or what?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D
utterances.text: I saw both. I had the opportunity of seeing both of them.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, you've also told us that you saw groups of mortars. Did you ever observe mortars being fired from your side of the confrontation lines?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was there any occasion when you saw mortars being fired from a position in the area of the Transit Road?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When was that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D
utterances.text: I don't know when this was exactly. During that period, from June 1992 until May 1993, that's the period that is concerned.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Are you able to be any more specific as to when it was during that period you made that observation? I'll withdraw that question. I'll ask you a different question first. On how many occasions did you see mortars being fired from the vicinity of the Transit Road?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D
utterances.text: I saw this very frequently.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Approximately when was the last occasion you saw that happening?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D
utterances.text: I can say that this was just before my departure.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Within days, weeks, or months?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D
utterances.text: It was a matter of a few days.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Whereabouts did you see the mortars being fired? That is, where were they when they were being fired?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D
utterances.text: There were mortars at various locations, in various positions.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was there ever an occasion when you noticed anything unusual about the crew firing mortars, that is, in the period whilst you were a member of the platoon?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D
utterances.text: Yes. I had the opportunity of seeing -- at one position I saw a crew which was often very drunk. Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were they firing mortars at the time that you observed them to be drunk, or not?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: On how many occasions did you see that happen?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D
utterances.text: Several times.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Approximately when was the last time that you saw that happen?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D
utterances.text: Are you referring to these men whom I saw under the influence of alcohol? Are you asking me when I saw them for the last time in such an alcoholised state?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D
utterances.text: I think that was in October or November 1992.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Where was the position they were firing from at that time?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D
utterances.text: They were in the vicinity of a bridge on the Transit Road.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You've told us that in about June of 2001 you were on the Transit Road with investigator Jonathan Tait-Harris. At that time, did you say anything to him in relation to this incident?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you then observe him to take a photograph?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D
utterances.text: Yes, I did. I saw him. I had previously shown him a location where the mortars were positioned, and he took a photograph of this location.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: At a later time did you place a mark on the photograph?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D
utterances.text: Yes. I marked the location where the mortars were. I marked this location on the photograph.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Mr. President, I ask that the witness again be shown the photographs which commence at P3251, in particular, Annexure B.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: In order to avoid any misunderstanding, I see the number Exhibit P3252 on Annexure B. That's --

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: That's the one, Mr. President, and I notice that the signature has been covered. Therefore, I ask that it be placed on the overhead projector, Annexure B.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you recognise the photograph before you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And could you tell the Tribunal what it is?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D
utterances.text: On this photograph the place where the mortars were located has been marked with a pen.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Who made that mark?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D
utterances.text: I made the circle.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What does the circle depict?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D
utterances.text: As I said, it depicts the location where the mortars had been positioned.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Where were you at the time that you made your observation? That is, when you observed the mortars being fired, where were you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D
utterances.text: I was on the road which is to the left of the photograph.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you mean to the left of the photograph as you look at the photograph?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D
utterances.text: No. To the right side of the photograph. You can see the road to the right side, on the right side of the photograph. That is where I was when I saw the mortars being fired.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You told us you were present when the photograph was taken. Whereabouts was the photographer positioned, approximately, at the time that this photograph was taken?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D
utterances.text: The photographer was on the left side of the bridge, if you look -- if you are facing the south.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What was the photographer standing on at the time the photograph was taken? In other words, on the dirt, on a footpath, on a box, or what?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D
utterances.text: On the bridge. He was on the bridge.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What is the road on the bridge, that is, the name of the road?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D
utterances.text: It's Transit, the Transit Road.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: As we look at the photograph, there appears to be a road curving towards the camera and to the right, as one looks at the photograph. Can you explain the relationship between that road and the Transit Road? I think you mentioned a bridge.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D
utterances.text: The road that you can see on the right of the photograph is below the bridge. It goes beneath the bridge, beneath the Transit, the bypass road. The photograph was taken from the bridge, and the street that you can see on the right goes under the bridge.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Where was the bridge in relation to where you had seen on different occasions a tank or an APC discharging its weaponry?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D
utterances.text: On the right.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How far away, approximately?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D
utterances.text: More than a hundred metres. About a hundred metres.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, you say that on this occasion in 1992, that is, the last such occasion where you made your observations, you concluded that the mortar crew were under the influence of alcohol. Could you tell us what it was that you saw that led you to that conclusion, or heard?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D
utterances.text: I could come to this conclusion on the basis of conversations, the way they looked. There were a few bottles scattered around them. It was very clear that they were drunk. This was very clear from their conversation.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you mean conversation between whom?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D
utterances.text: When they spoke to each other, it was obvious that they were drunk, and they were quite jolly.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What was it about their conversation that led you to that conclusion?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D
utterances.text: Their way of speaking. Anyone can notice this. When someone is drunk, they have slurred speech; they speak in a different manner.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You've told us that there were a number of occasions on which you had seen mortar crews operating the mortars, apparently affected by alcohol. On how many -- I withdraw that. Were there any other occasions that you saw such things in this position, apart from the one you've told us about?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D
utterances.text: Could you please repeat the question? I'm sorry.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you see a mortar crew apparently under the influence of alcohol operating mortars on other occasions in this position, from this position?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D
utterances.text: No, I didn't. I saw these men on several occasions. I saw them being in a drunken state on several occasions and I saw them using mortars. They were firing from mortars. But I didn't see this at any other.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: On how many different occasions did you see it happen at this position?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D
utterances.text: Several times. On five or six occasions.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: On this last occasion, how many rounds did you observe to be discharged from the mortar tubes?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D
utterances.text: I couldn't tell you exactly how many there were, but there were quite a few at any rate. At this point, I'm unable to remember how many shells were actually fired. But I'm sure that there were many.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you recollect the size of the mortar tubes?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D
utterances.text: No, I don't recollect the exact size, but I know that they were not of a small calibre, judging from the barrels from which the shells were fired. It must have been either an 80 or 120 millimetre calibre. I'm saying this because I was in a position to see mortars of smaller calibre which I believed to be 60 millimetre calibre mortars. These were much larger barrels.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you make any observations as to the degree of care with which they operated the mortars, that is, the mortar tubes?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D
utterances.text: Well, as careful as a drunk man can be and handle a weapon like that in such a state.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Having regard to your observations at the time, do you have any opinion as to whether they were capable of firing the mortars with any degree of accuracy given their physical and mental condition?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D
utterances.text: I'm sure that they were not capable enough for any precise targeting with this kind of weapon because they were in an inebriated state.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you observe -- withdraw that. How many tubes were they operating at that time?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D
utterances.text: There were three mortars there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How many of the three were operating?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D
utterances.text: All three of them were operating.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were you able to see what direction each of the tubes was pointing towards?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D
utterances.text: Yes, I was.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What direction was that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D
utterances.text: In the direction of the town, facing north.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Ierace, looking at the clock, I see that your indication that you might need one hour more than indicated, it's already more than one hour. And I don't know whether you could give any indication as to how much time you'd still need. And perhaps I may also draw your attention that according to the transcript, it took you approximately five minutes to get to the answer that the -- those who were drunk were approximately a hundred metres from the place where the APC and the tank were. Whether that really needed five minutes is a question still to be answered. But could you please give us an indication on how much time you still need.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: 10 minutes, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Ierace.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you have any particular feelings as you made your observations on this occasion?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What were they?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D
utterances.text: I felt terribly sorry that shells were being fired in such an unselective -- nonselective manner because I knew that they were killing people and damaging property.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Piletta-Zanin.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, in the English transcript, we are talking about a singular, and Mr. Ierace spoke on several -- spoke of several occasions of these mortars. I don't know if we are talking about singular or plural. Maybe my learned friend could clarify that for us, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I think if he used the plural, we have to assume that he intended to. But if it's otherwise, Mr. Ierace, you'll please tell us. And if not, please proceed.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Finally, sir, you have given evidence as to the existence of a sniper unit and conversations that you had with members of the sniping unit. Do you recall the names of any members of the sniping unit, in particular individuals who were members of the unit after September of 1992? Perhaps you might start with, if you know it, the name of their commander.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D
utterances.text: Yes, his name was Marinko Krneta.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you recall the names of any of the members during that period?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Please tell us the names.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D
