utterances.text: Miljenko Mitric, Dragan Zobenica, Nada, Predrag Boskovic, Zeljko Zelovic, Dragan Atanaskovic, Zlatko Subotic. At this point, I don't remember any other.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. And one further question: Would you please turn to -- withdraw that. Are you aware as to whether any military police operated in the area of Grbavica whilst you were a member of the platoon?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D
utterances.text: Yes, there was military police.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Are you aware as to whether there were any civilian police operating in that area during that same time period?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D
utterances.text: Yes, there was also the civilian police.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: During the course of making your statement in 1997, were you asked questions as to whether each of those police services had headquarters in the Grbavica area?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did they have headquarters, that is, each of them, in the Grbavica area?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D
utterances.text: Yes, they did.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you mark those positions on a map in 1997?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Mr. President, might the witness be shown Map 4, that is the copy which has the signature obscured.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sir, did you mark -- withdraw that. Do you see in blue ink on the map the numbers 1 and 2? Alongside each number, I think there is a cross. Do you see those?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you place those marks on that map?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What do those marks depict?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D
utterances.text: Number 1 -- number 2, I'm sorry, depicts the location where the civilian police was and number 1 where the military police was.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is that still your recollection as to the positions?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Are there any markings on any of the maps that I have asked you about during your evidence today which are not consistent with your recollection as it stands today?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D
utterances.text: I think I have the same one in mind.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In relation to the other maps that you've been shown today as well, Maps 1, 3, and 5, are there any markings on those maps that were made by you in 1997 which are no longer consistent with your recollection?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D
utterances.text: I think that on one of the maps these headquarters were depicted, but I'm not sure. I don't remember.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Perhaps you're misunderstanding the question. Would you please go to Map 5. Do you recollect that I asked you about the markings on this map earlier today?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Are the positions of the various weaponry indicated on this map according to your recollection today as well as in 1997?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D
utterances.text: I'm sorry, but I really don't understand you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I'm simply asking whether the positions on the map in front of you Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. of the tanks, mortars, Howitzers, and so on, accord with your recollection today of where they were whilst you were a member of the platoon.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The interpreter didn't hear the witness. We assume it was a "yes."

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Would you please repeat that answer.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D
utterances.text: Yes. I said yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: All right. Mr. President, that completes the examination-in-chief. You will note that there are some photographs and one map that I have not taken the witness to. In the interests of saving time, I don't propose to rely upon them. I have the original booklet available for inspection by the -- by you, Mr. President, and Your Honours, as well as by the Defence, should you wish to see it. I propose to tender the photocopy of the booklet rather than the original. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Wouldn't it be easier just to tender into evidence not booklets I have not seen yet but just the photographs shown to the witness, especially since -- then we can also take out those photographs that have not been used. As far as I can see, that's P3254A and the same number B, and P3255, while 51, 52, and 53 have been shown to the witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: That's so, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then we'll finally decide on the admission into evidence at the end of the cross-examination. Ms. Pilipovic, you'll do the cross-examination or Mr. Piletta-Zanin? Please proceed, Mr. Piletta-Zanin.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, it is actually Ms. Pilipovic who will be doing the cross-examination of the witness, but in view of the difficulties that we had with double translations this time, I should like to be allowed to ask five or six questions, at the maximum, once my colleague has completed her cross-examination, and thank you in advance.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. So, Ms. Pilipovic, you're first, and we'll see at the end of your cross-examination what's still left.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour. Cross-examined by Ms. Pilipovic:

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness D, good afternoon.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D
utterances.text: Good afternoon.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sir, would you please tell me whether you have at any point in time given a statement to the investigators of the OTP?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D
utterances.text: Yes, I have.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D
utterances.text: In February 1997 and in June 2001. Sorry. In February 1997 and in -- I think it was in wintertime, in the winter of 2001, either in January or December 19 -- I'm not sure.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you remember when it was that you gave your last statement?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Ms. Pilipovic, may I remind you to put off your microphone when the witness is answering your questions, in order to fully respect the protective measures.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D
utterances.text: The last time I gave the statement was in the summer of 2001.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you remember the venue?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Where was it?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D
utterances.text: In Sarajevo. And then I made some amendments here.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You said you made some amendments?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D
utterances.text: Yes. I did it here in The Hague.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you explain to us the reasons why you were invited to come here?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D
utterances.text: Because there was not enough time to finish everything in Sarajevo.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Where did you do your military service?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D
utterances.text: In Bihac.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Once you completed your military service, did you ever go to any military training subsequently?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D
utterances.text: No, I did not.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness D, you told us that you had given a statement to the OTP investigator on the 21st, 22nd, and 23rd of February, 1997.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D
utterances.text: I said I had given my statement in February 1997. I was not specific as to the dates.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In response to a question put to you by my learned colleague, you said that you had been called up to join the reserve police force.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When was that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D
utterances.text: It was the autumn before the war, so it must have been the autumn of 1991.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Why were you called?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D
utterances.text: I was called to the reserve police force. They requested specifically that I should come because they needed me for the purposes of adequate ethnic composition of the force.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What was your obligation in respect of that? Were you duty-bound to report and become a member of the reserve police force? What was your obligation in that respect?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D
utterances.text: Our obligation was to patrol around the area that we were in charge of, to see to it that there were no incidents of any kind, and to avoid presence of armed individuals in the area, to prevent presence of armed individuals in the area, and to report any such incident to the police, because at the headquarters which were in charge of us, there was a professional police officer serving there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Where was the headquarters?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D
utterances.text: In Beogradska Street.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you be more specific, sir? Where exactly is Beogradska Street located? In which part of the town?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D
utterances.text: It is part of the neighbourhood called Grbavica 1, the area of Kovacici, that is.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: At that time --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: We didn't hear the question of the counsel.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were you issued any equipment on that occasion?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D
utterances.text: Yes, I was.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What was it?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D
utterances.text: An automatic rifle, 7.62 calibre.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How long did you remain in that reserve force?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D
utterances.text: For a couple of weeks.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What did you do after that? Did you leave the force? What happened?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D
utterances.text: I managed to leave the force, but it was on my personal insistence.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were you under any obligation to return the equipment that you had been given?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D
utterances.text: Yes, I was.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So you returned your automatic rifle when you left?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D
utterances.text: Of course.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In your statement -- on page 2 of your statement --

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] And Your Honour, I am referring to Document 000969513, paragraph 2.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: That's fine. But could you please quote so that the Prosecution can follow what you are confronting the witness with, and so that we also can know what is in there.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, page 3 of the statement, paragraph 2.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Ierace.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The document -- the English version is 00472767. That is, the statement which the witness gave to the investigators of the Tribunal in February.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Has the translation been provided? Yes, okay. Please proceed. Mr. Ierace, you found it or?

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: I have, Mr. President. It was after the date of the statement. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Okay. Please proceed, Ms. Pilipovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You state, I quote: "The tensions grew until around March the 2nd when the first barricades were set up. At the moment when it was happening, it was not clear who set up the barricades. It was not clear who set up the barricades. The town was blocked by men wearing black masks on their faces. The barricades were everywhere in the town, so people were not able to go to work that morning. Afterwards, it became clear that the barricades were set up by the SDS, although the SDS publicly distanced itself from this issue." Sir, would you please tell us who set up the barricades on the 2nd of March? Do you have any knowledge about that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please, Mr. Ierace.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Mr. President, I object on the grounds of relevance. I have deliberately not taken this witness to pages of history which my friends have. We have heard much of the events leading up to the outbreak of hostilities, and the question asked by my friend, in my respectful submission, for two reasons is irrelevant: Firstly, because it doesn't touch upon the evidence given by the witness during his examination-in-chief; and secondly, because it's of no assistance to the Trial Chamber in determining the issues before it. There has to be some relevance to the history. I withdraw that. There has to be some reference to the preconflict history. But in relation to this witness's testimony, and in particular, events preceding the 6th of April, it's simply not relevant. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Ms. Pilipovic, would you please respond.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, it is the position of the Defence that during the cross-examination, a witness can be examined about the issues which were testified about both during the examination-in-chief and also discussed in the statements given by the witness to the investigators of the Tribunal, which constitute the documents which were disclosed by the Prosecution to the Defence. As for the objection itself raised by my learned colleague, with respect to the relevance of these questions relating to the events of the 2nd of March, that is, 1992, the Defence believes that these questions are quite important in view of the background of the conflict. They are not only relevant, but they are necessary for the purposes of testing the credibility of the witness as well.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Ierace.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Mr. President, I for one would be grateful if my friend could explain that relevance. In what way are the events of March 1992 relevant to the issues before this Court other than as general background so as to set the scene? Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please respond, Ms. Pilipovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'll be glad to do that, Your Honour. The events which took place on the 2nd of March are relevant indeed because by checking these -- this information, it will be possible to establish what the background of the conflict was, the conflict which is interpreted by the Prosecutor in a different way; that is, that there had been a prior plan. And by asking this type of question in respect to this statement of the witness, the Defence intends to secure answers as to what the situation was, whether the allegations are true against General Galic as they are contained in the indictment. I have read the statement, and the witness finishes this passage by saying "Later, it became clear that the barricades were set up by the SDS." I simply wish to ask the witness who it was exactly who set up the barricades and why the conflict broke out in Sarajevo so that we will be able to establish the reasons and the background of the conflict on the basis of these questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: One moment, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Ms. Pilipovic, as we discussed earlier, the area of cross-examination, we can see clearly from Rule 90(H). Part (i) says that "Cross-examination shall be limited to the subject matter of the evidence in chief and matters affecting the credibility of the witness, and when the witness is able to give evidence relevant to the case for the cross-examining party to the subject matter of that case." That means that "limited to the subject matter of the evidence in chief" means the evidence given by the witness in this Court. That means that not as such the previous statement given by the witness in its entirety and is a subject -- is subject to cross-examination. Then the second category is the credibility of the witness, of course, credibility of his testimony given in this Court. And the third is where the witness is able to give evidence relevant to the case for the cross-examining party. That might be the case here, and that's what you explained to us. But then, subsection (ii) says that "Counsel shall put to the witness the nature of the case of the party for whom that counsel appears which is in contradiction of the evidence given by the witness." So that means you have to indicate to this witness on issues contradicting what your case will be, what your case is. And then you may put questions to him. I do not see that, but you assist me if I'm wrong, I do not see that the questions you just put to the witness are referring to any part of his testimony given in this court, but if I am mistaken, please assist me. Yes, I see you're nodding.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, my question concerning the 2nd of March was raised and linked to the answer provided by Witness D in response to a question when the conflict started. The witness said that the conflict started on the 6th of April, 1992. So my question concerning the 2nd of March was a foundation for the following question that I had in mind: If the tensions grew on the 2nd of March, could that be considered as the main cause for the conflict which subsequently broke out?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I would say that if it's not your case that the conflict started at another date than the 6th of April, because you are now diving into the history of the conflict, which has not been touched upon by the examination-in-chief, but if the witness has contradicted in one way or the other your case in this respect - and that's how I understood it - that you say his testimony seems to be that the conflict just started on the 6th of April, while there was a whole history, then please tell him what your case is, and then ask him questions about it.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. I can imagine that some of your questioning was concerning your case, but we have another problem, I'm afraid. It's already five minutes past 4.00. So this also will give you the opportunity perhaps to better prepare. And please look carefully to Rule 90(H) again and again, because, as I indicated before, the Chamber will more strictly apply Rule 90(H). We will resume tomorrow morning at 9.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Tuesday, the 22nd day of January 2002, at 9.00 a.m. 20 21 22 23 24 25
